title: Python Basics for DevOps
summary: The Python you actually need: dicts, lists, YAML/JSON, file I/O, and your first CLI tool.

sections.title: Setup: virtual environments
sections.body:
Always use a virtual environment. Never install packages globally.

```bash
# Create a venv for your project
cd ~/my-devops-scripts
python3 -m venv .venv

# Activate it (do this every time you work on the project)
source .venv/bin/activate   # Linux/Mac
# .venv\Scripts\activate    # Windows

# Your prompt changes to show (.venv)
# Install packages into the venv
pip install boto3 pyyaml kubernetes requests

# Save dependencies for the team
pip freeze > requirements.txt

# Recreate on another machine
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Deactivate when done
deactivate
```

For one-off scripts, use uv (faster, modern alternative):
```bash
pip install uv
uv run --with boto3 my_script.py
```

sections.title: The three data types you'll use 90% of the time
sections.body:
```python
# --- Strings ---
app_name = "argocd-server"
namespace = "argocd"

# f-strings are your best friend
print(f"Checking {app_name} in namespace {namespace}")

# Common string methods
print(app_name.upper())           # ARGOCD-SERVER
print(app_name.replace('-', '_')) # argocd_server
print(app_name.split('-'))        # ['argocd', 'server']
print(app_name.startswith('argo'))  # True

# Multi-line strings
query = """
    SELECT *
    FROM pods
    WHERE namespace = 'argocd'
"""

# --- Lists ---
pods = ["pod-a", "pod-b", "pod-c"]

# Iteration
for pod in pods:
    print(pod)

# List comprehension — very Pythonic
running = [p for p in pods if "a" in p]  # filter
upper = [p.upper() for p in pods]          # transform

# Append, extend, sort
pods.append("pod-d")
pods.extend(["pod-e", "pod-f"])
pods.sort()

# Slicing
first_two = pods[:2]
last_one  = pods[-1]

# --- Dicts ---
pod_info = {
    "name": "argocd-server-abc123",
    "namespace": "argocd",
    "status": "Running",
    "restarts": 0,
}

# Access
print(pod_info["name"])                    # KeyError if missing
print(pod_info.get("image", "unknown"))    # safe, returns default

# Check membership
if "status" in pod_info:
    print(pod_info["status"])

# Iteration
for key, value in pod_info.items():
    print(f"  {key}: {value}")

# Dict comprehension
status_map = {p: "Running" for p in pods}

# Nested (like JSON / k8s manifests)
manifest = {
    "apiVersion": "apps/v1",
    "kind": "Deployment",
    "metadata": {"name": "my-app", "namespace": "default"},
    "spec": {"replicas": 3}
}
print(manifest["metadata"]["name"])         # my-app
print(manifest.get("spec", {}).get("replicas", 1))  # safe nested access
```

sections.title: JSON and YAML — your daily file formats
sections.body:
```python
import json
import yaml  # pip install pyyaml
from pathlib import Path

# --- JSON ---
# Parse from string
raw = '{"name": "my-pod", "status": "Running"}'
data = json.loads(raw)
print(data["name"])  # my-pod

# Parse from file
with open("pod.json") as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Write to file
with open("output.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(data, f, indent=2)

# Pretty print for debugging
print(json.dumps(data, indent=2))

# --- YAML ---
# Parse from string
raw_yaml = """
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
"""
manifest = yaml.safe_load(raw_yaml)   # always use safe_load, never load()
print(manifest["metadata"]["name"])   # my-app

# Parse from file
with open("values.yaml") as f:
    values = yaml.safe_load(f)

# Write YAML
with open("output.yaml", "w") as f:
    yaml.dump(data, f, default_flow_style=False)

# Load multiple YAML docs (--- separated, like k8s multi-manifest files)
with open("manifests.yaml") as f:
    docs = list(yaml.safe_load_all(f))

# --- pathlib (modern file paths) ---
current = Path.cwd()
values_file = Path("helm-charts/my-app/values.yaml")

if values_file.exists():
    content = values_file.read_text()

# Iterate directory
for yaml_file in Path("manifests").glob("**/*.yaml"):
    print(yaml_file.name)
```

sections.title: argparse — proper CLI tools
sections.body:
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check Helm values for image tag issues."""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Check Helm values for unpinned image tags"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "values_file",
        type=Path,
        help="Path to values.yaml"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output", "-o",
        choices=["text", "json"],
        default="text",
        help="Output format (default: text)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--fail-on-latest",
        action="store_true",  # boolean flag
        help="Exit 1 if any image uses :latest tag"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--namespace", "-n",
        default="default",
        help="Kubernetes namespace (default: default)"
    )
    return parser.parse_args()

def main():
    args = parse_args()

    # Access parsed args
    print(f"Checking: {args.values_file}")
    print(f"Output format: {args.output}")
    print(f"Namespace: {args.namespace}")

    if not args.values_file.exists():
        print(f"ERROR: File not found: {args.values_file}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Your actual logic here...
    found_latest = False  # example

    if args.fail_on_latest and found_latest:
        sys.exit(1)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run it:
```bash
python3 check_images.py values.yaml --fail-on-latest -o json
python3 check_images.py --help  # auto-generated help
```

sections.title: Exercise: Helm values image tag checker
sections.body:
Write `check_images.py` that:

1. Accepts a values.yaml path as argument
2. Recursively searches for any key called `tag` or `image`
3. Flags values that are `latest`, empty, or missing a version pin
4. Prints a report
5. Exits 1 if any issues found (so it can be used in CI)

Skeleton:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse
import sys
import yaml
from pathlib import Path

def find_images(data, path=""):
    """Recursively walk a dict and find image-related keys."""
    issues = []
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        for key, value in data.items():
            current_path = f"{path}.{key}" if path else key
            if key in ("tag", "image") and isinstance(value, str):
                # TODO: check if value is 'latest', empty, or not pinned
                pass
            # TODO: recurse into nested dicts and lists
    elif isinstance(data, list):
        pass  # TODO: recurse into list items
    return issues

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Check Helm values for image tag issues")
    parser.add_argument("values_file", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--fail-on-issues", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with open(args.values_file) as f:
        values = yaml.safe_load(f)

    issues = find_images(values)

    if not issues:
        print("All image tags look good.")
    else:
        print(f"Found {len(issues)} issue(s):")
        for issue in issues:
            print(f"  {issue}")

    if args.fail_on_issues and issues:
        sys.exit(1)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Test with a values.yaml like:
```yaml
image:
  repository: nginx
  tag: latest        # should flag this

sidecar:
  image: busybox     # should flag this (no tag)
  tag: "1.36.1"      # this is fine
```
